subject: Post-call: multilingual model evals & next steps (FR/DE/JP)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Ng <andrew.ng@globexretail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: multilingual model evals & next steps (FR/DE/JP)

Hi Andrew — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery call: 

1) Goals we heard
- Improve localized search relevance and product description generation for EU stores (FR, DE) and selected APAC locales (JA).
- Keep average generation latency < 400ms for short completions, and cost under $0.004/token on average for production.
- Maintain or improve translation-quality and brand tone across locales; avoid regressions vs your current rule-based system.

2) Recommended evaluation plan (lightweight POC)
- Run automated quality evals (BLEU/chrF + human spot checks) across a 1k prompt set per locale. We’ll provide the prompt sets.
- Candidate models to test: Redwood-2-multilingual-7B (low-latency baseline), Llama-3-70B-8k-quant (best-quality candidate), and a quantized Llama variant for cost tradeoffs.
- Metrics: generation F1/chrF, latency p95, token cost, and a regression flag against your baseline.

3) Next steps / asks
- I’ll share the prompt sets and a quick benchmark report we ran on similar retail workloads (attached).
- Can you confirm priority locales (FR / DE / JA) and whether we should add any others?
- If OK, propose a 2-week POC where Redwood runs the evals on Dedicated capacity and we provide results + suggested model/config combos.

Attachments: redwood-eval-prompt-set-v1.csv (prompt set sample); benchmark-results-eu-apac.pdf (recent benchmark snapshot).

Thanks — I’ve cc’d Neha (solutions) and Vivek (prod infra) to support the POC planning.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0193

From: Andrew Ng <andrew.ng@globexretail.com>

Cc: Lina Perez <lina.perez@globexretail.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: multilingual model evals & next steps (FR/DE/JP)

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap. A few quick clarifications: 

- Latency: our production SLA is 300ms p95 for short completions (search snippets). Can the Redwood-2-multilingual-7B meet that on your hosted infra?
- Cost: are the cost numbers you quoted including tokenization differences for Japanese?
- Data residency & GDPR: for EU stores we need logs and eval data to remain in an EU region during the POC. Is that supported for the Dedicated option?

I attached a small localization sample (globex-localization-sample.xlsx) that shows typical inputs by locale.

If you can confirm the above, we’re happy to move forward with the POC. Our timeline target is end of April.

—Andrew
Director, ML Product | Globex Retail
andrew.ng@globexretail.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Ng <andrew.ng@globexretail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: multilingual model evals & next steps (FR/DE/JP)

Hi Andrew — great questions, answered inline: 

- Latency: Redwood-2-multilingual-7B on Dedicated (GPU-backed) hits ~220–330ms p95 for short completions in our retail traces; 300ms p95 is achievable with the right batching/autoscale policy. We’ll provision a capacity profile for your target SLA during the POC.
- Cost: tokenization differences are accounted for in our cost model; Japanese tends to have fewer tokens per character but different detokenization patterns — we’ll surface both tokenized and character-normalized cost in the report.
- Data residency: yes — Dedicated in EU regions keeps eval logs and artifacts in-region. For Private deployments we can do the same with KMS controls. We’ll provide the SOC2+GDPR checklist during onboarding.

Proposed immediate actions: 
1) Confirm locales: FR (fr-FR), DE (de-DE), JP (ja-JP) — please confirm if OK.
2) We’ll start the eval run once you confirm and provide any additional localization edge cases. Expected turnaround: 10 business days for automated runs + a 3-day human spot-check window.
3) I’ve attached the prompt set and our benchmark snapshot; here’s the eval checklist we’ll use: automated metrics (chrF, BLEU), human rating (fluency, brand-tone), latency/cost breakdown, and regression flags.

Dashboard & artifacts: https://redwood.console/evals/GX-2027-031/dashboard
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/GX-2027-031
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-eval-prompts

If that looks good I’ll send a short SOW and we can kick off the POC. 

—Marissa
